explanation: The Prime Meridian comes ashore near the port of Tema. Mapmakers jokingly call the spot at sea where the two lines cross Null Island.

claims.text: Ghana's coast lies due north of the point where the Equator meets the Prime Meridian.
The coasts of Togo, Nigeria and Gabon lie east of the Prime Meridian.
The Prime Meridian reaches the coast of Ghana near the port of Tema.
The point at sea where the Equator and the Prime Meridian cross is jokingly called Null Island.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Claims: every checkable statement is listed, distractors included; every claim is standard: none holds a number, a superlative or another C26 trigger, and the item is not counterintuitive. Datasets: geonames-cities: Tema, GH, 5.6698, -0.01657, on the meridian (c1, c3); Lomé, TG, 6.12874, 1.22154, shows Togo's coast east of it (c2). mledoze-countries: NGA latlng 10, 8 and GAB latlng -1, 11.75, both well east (c2). Rival test: Togo is the planted near-miss, because the meridian crosses its northern edge inland, but its coast lies east; Gabon sits on the Equator and Nigeria is the big Gulf of Guinea country. Against the key: nothing; the first land due north of the crossing is Ghana's coast. Regional: Equally new to most players; West Africans have an edge, and anyone can reason from the meridian's path south from Europe through Algeria. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. External evidence: none beyond the dataset; c4 is standard. Seed: 5 (hard): most players guess between the Gulf of Guinea countries. Counterintuitive: false. Doubts: none.
